new_statements.quote: [p. 396] Stress on some loanwords may not follow from otherwise predictable rules. [...] Example (3) shows the preservation of a liquid-obstruent sequence, a syllable (and word) final nasal, and final syllable stress. All of these features violate the system of phonological constraints that were operational in the precontact Lachixío phonological system. (3) kolcho!n [kolˈtʃoŋ] <b-- [kolˈtʃoŋ] 'colchón // mattress' [p. 399] In native words, only voiceless obstruents are permitted medially (after a stressed syllable) and only voiceless obstruents are permitted word-initially in monosyllables: CVTV and TV (*CVDV, *DV), where <T> represents any voiceless obstruent and <D> any voiced obstruent.

(3) kolcho!n [kolˈtʃóŋ] <b-- [kolˈtʃoŋ] 'colchón // mattress'' (only difference: the printed IPA carries an acute on the o, trivial); p. 399 'In native words, only voiceless obstruents are pe…
new_statements.rule_in_words: One primary stress per phonological word, on the lexical root: native words are CV́TV or TV́ with the stressed syllable preceding the medial (voiceless, often geminate) obstruent, i.e. a trochaic foot on the root; proclitics and enclitics are unstressed ([[proclitic [stressed root]] enclitic] per Bueno Holle 2019: 18 reporting Sicoli 2007). Word-final stress is foreign to the native system and survives only in unassimilated Spanish loans. In a bare disyllabic root this is penultimate stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Sicoli 1999 is silent. Bueno Holle 2019: 18, reporting Sicoli 2007: 'only primary (no secondary) stress which is non-iterative, that is, has at most one stress foot'.
new_statements.exceptions: Unassimilated Spanish loans may keep final-syllable stress (kolcho!n [kolˈtʃoŋ] 'mattress', jardin [xarˈdin] 'garden'); 'Stress on some loanwords may not follow from otherwise predictable rules' (p. 396). Assimilated loans take the native pattern (kalo [ˈkal:o] 'broth', sonaja [soˈnax:a] 'rattle').
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word (root plus clitics); the 1999 examples are isolated citation forms in a practical orthography with an acute accent marking stress and IPA with ˈ. The statement is indirect: Sicoli states that native words have a stressed syllable before the medial obstruent (CVTV) and that final stress violates native constraints; he never writes a one-line stress rule. Phrase-level emphasis (gemination/lengthening of the stressed foot) and boundary tones are described in Sicoli 2007 per Bueno Holle 2019: 18.
new_statements.identity_note: All opened sources describe the Zapotec of Santa María Lachixío (Sola de Vega district, Oaxaca), which Sicoli 1999: 395 calls 'a dialect of the Solteco branch'; this is Glottolog lach1249 / ISO zpl (also listed under Zimatlán/Western Zapotec names). Sicoli 2007 additionally covers Asunción Mixtepec Zapotec (zoo, asun1236); the Bueno Holle 2019 report concerns Lachixío only.

sources.note: No dedicated stress section, but first-hand phonological statements: 'Stress on some loanwords may not follow from otherwise predictable rules'; final-syllable stress in unassimilated loans 'violate[s] the system of phonological constraints that were operational in the precontact Lachixío phonological system' (p. 396); native words are CVTV/TV with voiceless obstruents 'medially (after a stressed syllable)' (p. 399); all transcribed disyllables carry stress on the first (penultimate) syllable, e.g. bexo ['veʃ:o], texa ['teʃ:a], sonaja [so'nax:a] (pp. 399-400).

sources.citation: Bueno Holle, Juan José (2019). Information structure in Isthmus Zapotec narrative and conversation (Topics at the Grammar-Discourse Interface 3). Berlin: Language Science Press. Section 2.2.2, pp. 18-19
sources.note: Second-hand report of Sicoli 2007: 'He describes Lachixío Zapotec as a "stress-timed" language where there is only primary (no secondary) stress which is non-iterative, that is, has at most one stress foot.... The maximal phonological word is composed of a clitic phrase with the following structure: [[proclitic [stressed root]] enclitic]. The metrical foot, the unit counted for rhythm, is trochaic.' Emphasis marked by geminate medial consonant or lengthened stressed vowel of the primary foot (p. 18).
